reason: abbrev for CategoryTheory.Category C, which is exactly the book's notion of a category (objects, Hom classes, associative composition, unit morphisms). Faithful delegation to Mathlib.
Pure notational convention (write X in C instead of X in Ob(C)). No mathematical content to formalize; nothing dropped.

Six example instances exhibiting Sets, Groups, Rings, Vect_k, A-mod, Top as categories via inferInstance. These are real Mathlib category instances, not vacuous. Homotopy category (6) omitted but the listed instances faithfully cover items 1-5.
abbrev for P.FullSubcategory (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory), the full subcategory cut out by an object predicate with Hom_{C'}=Hom_C. Matches the book definition.

The book claims AbelianGroups is a FULL SUBCATEGORY of Groups. The Lean statement only asserts `Category CommGrpCat` (that abelian groups form a category), which is strictly weaker; it does not assert the fully-faithful forgetful embedding CommGrpCat -> GrpCat. The full-subcategory relationship (the actual content) is only described in the docstring, which is not evidence.
dropped_conjunct: the full/fully-faithful embedding CommGrpCat into GrpCat (the subcategory being FULL)

reason: Asserts ModuleCat k is k-linear (Hom spaces are k-modules), i.e. enriched over k-Vect. Faithful to the claim that Rep(A) is enriched over k-vector spaces.
abbrev for CategoryTheory.Functor C D, which packages the object map plus Hom map preserving composition and identities. Exactly the book definition.

reason: Exhibits forgetful functors Groups->Sets, Rings->Sets, and the Hom functor Y -> Hom(X,Y) as real Functor terms. The book lists 9 illustrative examples; the formalized subset (items 2 and 4) are faithful witnesses. Illustrative example list, not a single claim; no conjunct silently weakened.

abbrev for CategoryTheory.NatTrans F G, the collection of components a_X with the naturality square a_Y o F(f) = G(f) o a_X. Matches the book; isomorphism-of-functors notion is Mathlib NatIso as noted.

double_dual_iso gives V ≃ V** for finite-dimensional V (Module.evalEquiv); double_dual_naturality asserts the genuine naturality square f.dualMap.dualMap o eval = eval o f. Together they faithfully capture item (1): id and ** are isomorphic functors on FVect_k. Real content (an actual iso plus a naturality equation), not vacuous. Items 2-4 not formalized but the central claim is.
abbrev for CategoryTheory.Equivalence C D, which packages F, F', and natural isomorphisms F o F' ≅ id, F' o F ≅ id. Exactly equivalence/quasi-inverse from the book.

States ∃! (a : X ≅ Y), yoneda.map a.hom = phi.hom for an iso phi : yoneda.obj X ≅ yoneda.obj Y. This is precisely the book's claim that an iso of representable functors induces a unique iso X ≅ Y, proved via Yoneda.fullyFaithful. Real existence-and-uniqueness, not a trivial Nonempty. (Uses contravariant yoneda Hom(?,X) rather than Hom(X,?); this is only a variance convention and the uniqueness content is identical.)
Expository remark noting representable functors generalize to enriched settings. No formalizable claim; nothing dropped.

Gives the equivalence (R ->l[R] M) ≃l[ℕ] M (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf), i.e. Hom_R(R,M) ≅ M, exhibiting the forgetful functor as represented by the regular module R. Faithful to the positive claim. The negative claim (not representable for inf-dim A on f.d. modules) is not formalized, as expected for a counterexample remark.
abbrev for CategoryTheory.Adjunction F G, which encodes the natural hom-set isomorphism Hom_D(F X, Y) ≅ Hom_C(X, G Y) functorial in X and Y. Exactly the book definition of adjoint pair.
Motivational analogy (category theory vs inner product spaces dictionary). No formalizable mathematical claim; nothing dropped.

frobenius_reciprocity gives Rep.indFunctor ⊣ Rep.resFunctor (real Adjunction, item 2). uea_adjunction gives the hom-set bijection (L ->l⁅R⁆ A) ≃ (U(L) ->a[R] A) (item 3). Both are genuine adjunction content, not Nonempty placeholders. Illustrative list; items 1,4,5 unformalized but the formalized ones are faithful.

abbrev for CategoryTheory.Abelian C. Mathlib's intrinsic definition (preadditive, has kernels/cokernels, normal monos/epis) is provably equivalent to the book's embedding-into-A-mod definition via Freyd-Mitchell, and is the standard faithful encoding. Real class, not vacuous.
Asserts ModuleCat A is abelian via inferInstance. Faithful to the claim that A-mod is an abelian category. (Finite-dimensional subcategory not separately stated, but the principal claim is covered.)

Remark 7.7.4 itself is expository prose about the drawback of Definition 7.7.1 (the ring A is not determined by C; Morita equivalence) with no formalizable mathematical claim. The adjacent Discussion file appropriately formalizes a related fact (A-mod is k-linear over a field k) via inferInstance. Nothing from the remark's content is dropped because there is nothing assertable to formalize.

abbrev for CochainComplex C ℤ (HomologicalComplex with ComplexShape.up ℤ), encoding objects C_i, differentials d_i, and d ∘ d = 0. Faithful to the complex/differential definition. Cohomology/exactness are Mathlib HomologicalComplex.homology as noted; the formalized object is the complex itself, which is the core datum.

abbrev for CategoryTheory.ShortComplex C; a short exact sequence is a ShortComplex with ShortExact (mono f, epi g, exact middle), as the docstring notes and Mathlib provides. Faithful encoding of 0 -> X -> Y -> Z -> 0.

Proves (ShortComplex.mk biprod.inl biprod.snd).ShortExact for X ⊞ Z via ShortComplex.Splitting.ofHasBinaryBiproduct. This is the genuine split SES 0 -> X -> X⊞Z -> Z -> 0 of the book, with a real proof. Not vacuous.

connectingHomomorphism is hS.delta (snake-lemma connecting map H^i(X3) -> H^j(X1)). The three exactness theorems assert genuine exactness at each position of the long exact sequence (homology_exact₁/₂/₃). Real content fully matching the book's c_i and long exact sequence of cohomology.

abbrev for CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F (induces additive maps on Hom groups). Matches the book's additive-functor definition. (k-linear part is referenced via Functor.Linear in the docstring but not separately abbreviated; the additive notion, the primary def, is faithful.)

Two instances: restrictScalars f is Functor.Additive and (along an algebra hom) Functor.Linear R0. These are real instances underlying Res being additive/k-linear. Faithful illustrative witnesses; Ind and Hom_G(V,-) not separately formalized but the example is an illustrative list.

abbrevs for PreservesFiniteLimits (left exact) and PreservesFiniteColimits (right exact). In an abelian category, preserving finite limits is equivalent to preserving exactness of 0->X->Y->Z (and dually), the standard faithful encoding of the book's definition.

def : Prop = ∀ S : ShortComplex C, S.ShortExact -> Nonempty S.Splitting. Non-vacuous: ShortExact is a real hypothesis and Splitting is genuine data (a splitting is exactly isomorphism to 0->X->X⊞Y->Y->0). Faithfully captures 'every SES splits'. The Nonempty wraps real splitting data, not a trivial witness, so it passes the anti-vacuity test.

Proves IsSemisimpleRing (MonoidAlgebra k G) under IsUnit (card G : k) for a finite group. This is Maschke's theorem at ring level; semisimplicity of the ring is equivalent to semisimplicity of the module/representation category. Faithful with the correct char-not-dividing-|G| hypothesis. Real proof.

hom_left_exact: PreservesFiniteLimits (coyoneda.obj (op X)) = Hom(X,-) left exact (ii). tensor_right_exact: PreservesFiniteColimits (tensorLeft X) = X ⊗ - right exact (iii). Both real instances faithful to the positive claims. The 'not right/left exact' counterexamples and item (i) Ind/Res exactness are not formalized, as expected for negative illustrative remarks.
